insight: Ecuador's performance in the 2026 World Cup shows that hydration breaks have a significant impact on their momentum, with the team gaining momentum in 6 out of 8 breaks, indicating a slight increase in their performance after the breaks. When Ecuador was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with an average change of -0.200 minutes, only managing to keep their momentum 2 out of 4 times. In contrast, when they were not pressing before a break, they actually gained momentum, with an average change of +0.075 minutes, suggesting that the breaks allowed them to regroup and come back stronger. Overall, these statistics suggest that Ecuador benefits from hydration breaks, especially when they are not exerting high pressure before the break, as it gives them an opportunity to recover and regain their energy.
